items.title: analyze-batch.mjs emits a three-state H1-H4 report.json + report.md
items.context: Offline analyzer reads batch-ledger.jsonl (H1/H4), tamper-verdicts.jsonl (H2), resume-reconciliation.json (H3), and protocol.json; adjudicates each hypothesis to pass|fail|inconclusive with the supporting numbers; writes report.json + a human-readable report.md. Never re-executes the instrument or calls the lattice CLI.
items.userSees: node analyze-batch.mjs prints 'H1 replay-determinism: pass', 'H2 tamper-fail-closed: pass', 'H3 resume-integrity: pass', 'H4 scale-envelope: pass', 'overall: all-pass', 'digest: <sha256>' and writes report.json + report.md.

happy.desc: node experiments/pos-instrument-replay/analyze-batch.mjs reads the four committed evidence streams + protocol.json, adjudicates H1/H2/H3/H4 to three-state verdicts (all pass on the current evidence), prints overall all-pass + a digest, and writes report.json + report.md

edge.desc: a scale with <2 proof records, or an absent/empty hypothesis input, yields inconclusive (NOT pass) for that hypothesis

adversarial.desc: a non-conforming tamper verdict / an over-cap elapsedMs / gapTotal>0 flips the corresponding hypothesis to fail — never a false pass

verificationEvidence.note: node analyze-batch.mjs (offline, only fs/path/url + lib/instrument.mjs) re-verifies each batch-ledger recordDigest then STRICTLY adjudicates: H1 requires exactly protocol.N[scale] well-formed (non-empty digests+goldMetrics) pairwise-equal records per scale; H2 requires the (class,handling) identity set == protocol.tamperMatrix + per-row conformance + dispositionMatch; H3 requires the substantive killA/B/C+protocolReplaySmallCount+hypothesis fields; H4 requires finite non-negative elapsedMs <= cap. On the real evidence all four = pass, overall all-pass, digest f4224085e06db3a421bf6d6eed6204733d277696f1225403d03ab264bf3fd3ba; writes report.json + report.md.

Strict three-state closes the round-1 false-pass holes: an incomplete scale (fewer than protocol.N records), stripped digests/goldMetrics, a missing tamper (class,handling) identity, a 3-field resume stub, or a negative/null elapsedMs each now flip the corresponding hypothesis to FAIL (never a false pass) — proven by selfcheck-m4 sub-checks J/K/L/M/N; an absent input file yields inconclusive + a null generatedInputs sha (never a crash, never all-pass) — sub-check O.
selfcheck-m4 sub-check G: an empty resume-reconciliation.json yields H3=inconclusive (not pass, not a crash) and overall=some-inconclusive — the missing-evidence edge is handled as inconclusive.

items.title: report carries a reproducible digest; re-run is byte-identical
items.context: report.digest = sha256(canonicalJson(report minus the digest field)), reusing lib/instrument.mjs sha256/canonicalJson. Running analyze-batch.mjs twice on the same committed inputs yields byte-identical report.json + report.md + digest (deterministic, offline).
items.userSees: Running node analyze-batch.mjs twice on the same committed inputs prints the identical 'digest: <sha256>' and produces byte-identical report.json + report.md.

happy.desc: two consecutive runs of node analyze-batch.mjs on the same committed inputs produce byte-identical report.json, report.md, and digest

edge.desc: the report records each input file sha256 and the protocol sha256 so the digest is bound to the exact evidence it adjudicated

adversarial.desc: digest = sha256(canonicalJson(report minus the digest field)); re-deriving it from the emitted report.json by hand matches, and there is no timestamp/random value in the digested preimage (would break cross-host replication)

verificationEvidence.note: Reproducible: two runs of analyze-batch.mjs on the committed inputs produce byte-identical report.json + the digest f4224085e06db3a421bf6d6eed6204733d277696f1225403d03ab264bf3fd3ba; digest = sha256(canonicalJson(report minus the digest field)) — independently re-derived by hand (sorted-key canonical JSON, sha256) and by Codex host-2, both matching. No Date/random/absolute-path in the digested preimage.

selfcheck-m4 sub-check B runs the sandboxed analyzer twice and asserts report.json is byte-identical (Buffer.equals) and the digest is identical across runs — reproducibility is machine-verified, not just re-printed.

selfcheck-m4 sub-check I: in a fail case the report omits the claim field and the digest is still computed and present, so the digest is defined for non-all-pass reports too (order-independent over canonicalJson).

items.title: hermetic selfcheck-m4.mjs proves the three-state logic is un-gameable + Codex replicates the digest
items.context: selfcheck-m4.mjs asserts each hypothesis pass/fail/inconclusive is derived correctly, and that tampered/truncated/missing/insufficient evidence yields inconclusive or fail (NEVER a false pass); asserts digest reproducibility. A genuine Codex host-2 pass independently re-derives the report digest from the same inputs.
items.userSees: node selfcheck-m4.mjs prints 'selfcheck-m4 PASS' and exits 0; a genuine Codex host-2 run re-derives the same report digest offline.

happy.desc: node experiments/pos-instrument-replay/selfcheck-m4.mjs exits 0 and prints selfcheck-m4 PASS

edge.desc: selfcheck-m4 covers each hypothesis: a well-formed evidence set yields the expected pass, and an insufficient one yields inconclusive

adversarial.desc: selfcheck-m4 mutates evidence per hypothesis (flip a dispositionMatch / over-cap an elapsedMs / set gapTotal>0 / remove a hypothesis input) and asserts the verdict flips to fail or inconclusive — NEVER a false pass; and asserts digest reproducibility across two runs. Codex host-2 independently re-derives the report digest from the same inputs.

verificationEvidence.note: node selfcheck-m4.mjs exits 0 'selfcheck-m4 PASS' — sub-checks A-O: A-happy, B-reproducible, C/D/E/F (H1/H2/H3/H4 flip to fail on value mutation), G (empty input inconclusive), H (recordDigest-tamper abort), I (no-overclaim), + J h1-incomplete, K h1-vacuous, L h2-identity-missing, M h3-stub, N h4-negative/null, O absent-file-inconclusive.

Un-gameable + cross-host. selfcheck-m4 sub-checks A-I: A-happy (all-pass), B-reproducible (two runs byte-identical digest), C-h1-fail / D-h2-fail / E-h3-fail / F-h4-fail (each mutation flips its hypothesis to fail — never a false pass), G-inconclusive (removing an input -> inconclusive not pass), H-integrity-abort (a naively-edited ledger record without a recomputed recordDigest -> analyze-batch exits 1 naming the offending iterationId, no all-pass report), I-no-overclaim (fail case omits the claim text). CROSS-HOST: genuine Codex gpt-5.5 host-2 independently (1) ran analyze-batch -> digest a5f07cfaa4edb99a9064efae0ed7462f1fbca76a9bef693f7ffe208eed691f05, (2) RE-DERIVED that digest from report.json by hand (remove digest field, recursively-sorted-key canonical JSON, sha256) -> identical, (3) confirmed offline (no subprocess) -> 'DIGEST REPLICATED: YES'.
selfcheck-m4 sub-check I confirms the no-overclaim edge: a failed report.md omits the claim text and states 'Claim NOT asserted', and report.json omits the claim field.

items.title: analyze-batch.mjs re-verifies each input record's integrity (per-record recordDigest; abort with the offending id on mismatch) before adjudication, and report.json/.md include the scale-envelope numbers (elapsed/endOfRunRss per scale), the section-3 claim text verbatim only when overall is all-pass, and any instrument defect found
items.context: Covers execution-plan gaps flagged by the scope-plan review: §6.2/§6.4/§9 input-integrity — re-derive each batch-ledger record's recordDigest = sha256(canonicalJson(record minus recordDigest)) and refuse with the named iterationId on any mismatch (detects a naively-edited ledger) BEFORE adjudicating; §10/§3 no-overclaim — embed the section-3 claim text verbatim in report.md ONLY when all four hypotheses are supported, otherwise state plainly which are fail/inconclusive; §12 DoD — the report lists any instrument defect found (none when clean); §7 artifact table — report includes the per-scale scale-envelope numbers (max elapsedMs, peak endOfRunRss). Makes the analyzer tamper-detecting and the report self-contained + non-overclaiming.
items.userSees: report.md shows the H1-H4 verdicts, per-scale scale-envelope numbers (max elapsedMs / peak RSS), and — only when overall is all-pass — the verbatim section-3 claim text; a naively-edited ledger record makes analyze-batch abort with that record's iterationId (nonzero exit) instead of emitting a report.

happy.desc: analyze-batch re-verifies every batch-ledger recordDigest + tamper-verdict integrity, then writes report.md containing the per-scale scale-envelope numbers and (all-pass case) the verbatim section-3 claim text + an empty instrument-defect list

edge.desc: when a hypothesis is fail/inconclusive the report OMITS the section-3 claim text and states plainly which hypotheses are unmet (no-overclaim)

adversarial.desc: editing a single batch-ledger record field (breaking its recordDigest) makes analyze-batch ABORT with that record iterationId (nonzero), never emitting a pass report; selfcheck-m4 asserts this input-integrity refusal

verificationEvidence.note: Pre-adjudication integrity: analyzer re-derives every ledger recordDigest (all 33 re-derive) and verifies protocol.json sha256 == protocol.json.sha256; report.json/.md carry per-scale scaleEnvelope (small maxElapsedMs=2382/peakRss=174112768; full 18718/976666624), the §3 claim verbatim (only because overall=all-pass), and instrumentDefects=[] (clean).

selfcheck-m4 sub-check I: when overall is NOT all-pass the §3 claim text is withheld from report.md/.json and 'Claim NOT asserted' is emitted with the unmet hypotheses — the verbatim-claim-only-on-all-pass rule (plan §10) is enforced.

Input-integrity + no-overclaim intact after hardening: a batch-ledger record edited without a recomputed recordDigest makes analyze-batch abort (exit 1) naming the offending iterationId (sub-check H); report.md embeds the section-3 claim ONLY when overall all-pass (sub-check I); report includes per-scale scale-envelope numbers + empty instrumentDefects.
